title: Cohomology over an affine base is the global sections of the higher direct images
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], and assume that $S$ is affine [def-pc-scheme]. For every integer $q\geq0$ and every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent] there is an isomorphism of abelian groups
$$
e_{\mathcal F}:\;\Gamma\bigl(S,R^qf_*\mathcal F\bigr)=H^0\bigl(S,R^qf_*\mathcal F\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q(X,\mathcal F),
$$
where $H^q(X,-)$ is the cohomology of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $R^qf_*$ the $q$-th higher direct image [pqf-def-cohomology]; these isomorphisms are natural in $\mathcal F$: for every morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules, $e_{\mathcal G}\circ\Gamma(S,R^qf_*\varphi)=H^q(X,\varphi)\circ e_{\mathcal F}$. (The source states it for $f$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the separated case is the one stated here.)
